articles.title: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
articles.summary: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
articles.summaryTr: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.
articles.articleText: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine - Published Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making. Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort. The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before". Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partially resumed on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - after they had been closed following Russian strikes overnight. Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good. While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin. The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight. The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014. The $3.6bn (£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018. In Ukraine, the much-hated bridge is seen as one of the main symbols of Russia's continuing occupation of Ukrainian lands. "We're drinking champagne!" Andrii, an engineer who lives in Kyiv, told the BBC. He said the latest attack would "deal a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians". Some Ukrainians are concerned that Putin might now respond by carrying out even more attacks against civilian infrastructure, but Andrii said: "I don't think the Russians can make things much worse; they're already pounding us every single night with everything they've got." The damage after the overnight attack, involving cruise missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section apparently destroyed. Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below. Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective". He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage". The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed. Ukraine's state security service SBU said its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders". Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch. The Kremlin said Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China. Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations". For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday. In Kyiv, loud explosions were heard just before midnight on Monday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies. On Tuesday, Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had targeted the Southern Bridge, and another three had been fired on the Northern Bridge. Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were also damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters. Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River, connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials. The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear, though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly. The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired. However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar. This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo. There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack. Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area. In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. Additional reporting by Jaroslav Lukiv Related topics - Published5 hours ago

articles.title: Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board
articles.summary: Russia's defence ministry says it preliminarily believes a technical malfunction was the cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board
articles.summaryTr: Russia's defence ministry says it preliminarily believes a technical malfunction was the cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.
articles.articleText: Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board - Published A Russian military transport plane has crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, the country's defence ministry said, according to state-run media. The An-12 aircraft went down during a "scheduled flight" in an "uninhabited area" in the Kemerovo region, the ministry said in a statement. The ministry added that it preliminarily believed a technical malfunction was the cause of Tuesday's crash. An investigation by Russia's aviation authorities is now under way. Local Governor Ilya Seredyuk said an emergency response team "quickly extinguished a blaze" after the crash near the village of Yagunovo, and the area was sealed off by police. Seredyuk, who visited the crash site, said "a helicopter and medical facilities have been put on standby". The governor added that the "main task" now was to help investigators carry out their work. He also posted a video showing firefighters combing through what looked like the crash debris, with a number of ambulances also seen standing nearby. CCTV footage posted on social media appeared to show the moment the plane crashed, with a lighted object falling through the sky in the distance. An explosion then lit up the sky, but the crash was too far away to be seen. The BBC and Reuters news agency verified the time and date of the footage, while Reuters also verified the location based on features of the scenery that matched satellite imagery of the area. It was not immediately known whether the crashed aircraft had any cargo on board. An-12 planes are widely used by the Russian military to transport weaponry and personnel, and also for search and rescue operations.

articles.titleTr: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
articles.summaryTr: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.
articles.articleText: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers - Published After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months. Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination". The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines. The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s. The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections. The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness. PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year. "These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination." He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission. Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, said that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates. US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr Kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to US vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years. Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections. Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status". "Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency said. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans. "Vaccination does," she said. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities." In a post on social media, Kennedy said: "I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles." "We are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust," he also said. "We will answer families' questions honestly about vaccine benefits and risks and work with trusted health care providers and community leaders to prevent measles, limit its spread, and support timely treatment." The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Nuwan Gunawardhana, an assistant professor of medicine with Columbia University Irving Medical Center, said the US losing its elimination status was "a huge leap backwards". The US was the first country to eliminate measles in the Americas thanks to vaccination campaigns, noted William Moss, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. Dr Gunawardhana said it took massive efforts from public health officials and clinicians to build trust with patients to increase uptake of the MMR vaccine, leading to decades in the US with few infections and deaths. But that trust has been steadily eroding since the Covid-19 pandemic, when Dr Gunawardhana said patients were confronted with misinformation about the safety of vaccines and lost even more trust in public health systems. The vaccination rate for MMR across the US has fallen to 92.4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects those who cannot get vaccinated, including newborns. An outbreak in Pennsylvania has infected over 1,400 people - likely a large underestimate - and killed seven people, according to state officials. Kennedy, the health secretary, has sparred with Pennsylvania officials over how it is counting the measles deaths, with CDC declining for now to record some of the deaths in its database. Last year, the health secretary fired all the members of a top vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with his own appointees, some of whom were vaccine critics. The panel recommended a number of vaccine changes - including no longer requiring the Hepatitis B vaccine for all newborns - but those recommendations were blocked by a federal judge. President Donald Trump this year also cast doubt on the safety of the MMR vaccine, issuing an executive order for the shot to be split into three separate immunisations for measles, mumps and rubella, a move public health experts say is costly and could sow confusion about an already safe vaccine. Doctors and public health officials say the misinformation from Kennedy and Trump has played a major role in falling vaccination rates. "It's confusing patients. It's confusing families," Dr Gunawardhana said. "We need a clear message from the top." articles.summaryTr: ABD'de FEMA'nın ülke çapındaki acil durum sistemi testi sırasında televizyon ve radyo yayınları kısa süreliğine kesildi. Yaklaşık bir dakika süren testte cep telefonlarına bildirim gönderilmedi.
articles.articleText: ABD'de ekranlar karardı, yayınlar kesildi: FEMA ülke çapında acil durum testi yaptı - ABD'de FEMA'nın ülke çapındaki acil durum sistemi testi sırasında televizyon ve radyo yayınları kısa süreliğine kesildi. Yaklaşık bir dakika süren testte cep telefonlarına bildirim gönderilmedi. ABD Federal Acil Durum Yönetim Ajansı (FEMA), ülke genelinde kullanılan Acil Durum Uyarı Sistemi'nin (EAS) işleyişini değerlendirmek amacıyla kapsamlı bir test gerçekleştirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Federal İletişim Komisyonu (FCC) koordinasyonunda yapılan test, ABD Doğu Saati'ne göre 14.20'de başladı. Uygulama kapsamında binlerce televizyon kanalı, radyo istasyonu, kablolu yayın ve uydu hizmeti sağlayıcısının yayınları kısa süreliğine kesildi. İzleyici ve dinleyicilere önce tanıdık acil durum uyarı sesleri iletildi, ardından bunun rutin bir test olduğunu belirten yaklaşık bir dakikalık mesaj yayınlandı. Cep telefonlarına bu kez bildirim gönderilmedi Test kapsamında yalnızca televizyon ve radyo üzerinden çalışan Acil Durum Uyarı Sistemi değerlendirildi. Cep telefonlarına doğrudan gönderilen Kablosuz Acil Durum Uyarıları (WEA) ise bu yılki uygulamanın dışında bırakıldı. 2023 yılında gerçekleştirilen son ülke çapındaki testte hem televizyon ve radyo yayınları hem de cep telefonu bildirimleri kullanılmıştı. Amaç ulusal acil durumlarda iletişimi güvence altına almak FEMA'nın gerçekleştirdiği testle, ulusal acil durumlarda halkın hızlı ve doğru bilgilendirilmesini sağlayan iletişim altyapısının güvenilirliği ölçüldü. Sistem; ulusal güvenlik tehditleri, şiddetli hava olayları, tahliye kararları ve kamu güvenliğini ilgilendiren diğer acil gelişmelerde yetkililerin halka ulaşmasını sağlıyor. Testte yayıncı kuruluşların teknik altyapıları, uyarı mesajlarının iletimi ve sistemlerin çalışma kapasitesi değerlendirildi. ABD'deki kesintilerin ardından dikkat çeken test ABD'de son dönemde havacılık, bankacılık ve teknoloji sistemlerinde yaşanan çeşitli kesintilerin ardından gerçekleştirilen uygulama, ülkenin iletişim altyapısının güvenilirliğini yeniden gündeme taşıdı. FEMA, testin önceden planlandığını ve yaklaşan bir ulusal acil durumun işareti olmadığını vurguladı. Federal yasalar uyarınca ABD'nin acil durum uyarı sisteminin en az üç yılda bir ülke çapında test edilmesi gerekiyor.

articles.titleTr: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
articles.summaryTr: The Metropolitan Police say he has been taken into custody by the US Military over suspected national security and espionage allegations.
articles.articleText: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody - Published A US Army officer arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia earlier this month has been taken into US military custody, British counter-terror police have said. The serviceman has been identified as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, BBC News understands. The 41-year-old - who has served in the US Army since 2008 - was arrested near Gloucester last week by British counter-terror police. Tyner was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC). Counter Terror Policing said he is now in custody over suspected national security and espionage allegations. At the time of his arrest, Russia said they had "nothing to do with it". British police previously said he was being held in London after he was arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023, which relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service. The day after Tyner's arrest, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he was "unaware" of what it was connected to. "We have nothing to do with it, and it has nothing to do with us," he told reporters in Moscow. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said: "Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them [their American partners] to progress." "These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," he added. FBI director Kash Patel said an army officer was in custody "as the result of an espionage investigation and the close cooperation" between the bureau, US Army and various UK partners. "Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action," he said. "This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk." US Brig Gen Sean Stinchon said the case should serve as a "stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath" they all take. "Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardising our collective defence, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served," he added. articles.titleTr: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
articles.summaryTr: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
articles.articleText: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says - Published A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says. There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority. According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman. There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost. They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control. All settlements are illegal under international law. - UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements - Published3 hours ago Local Palestinians said that the events in al-Duyuk al-Tahta on Monday night began with harassment by Israeli settlers. Palestinian children threw stones, they said, and the settlers opened fire, killing Fadda al-Fahidat, who was 72, outside her home. Fadda's daughter-in-law, Nema al-Fahidat, told the BBC that she died from a single bullet wound to the head. "It destroyed her brain," she said. According to the Palestinian accounts, Fadda's son, Arafat, rushed to the scene in his car after hearing the news and collided with an empty Israeli settler car parked outside his family home, injuring settlers who were standing nearby. The settlers then fired more shots, they said, injuring several Palestinians, including Arafat. "My husband, when he saw his mother, was not paying attention. He crashed into the vehicle. The vehicle was empty," Nema said. "My husband got out of his car and tried to reach his mother and the injured young men. Then he was shot." She added: "We tried to gather the injured people and move them away from the settler. We brought them here. But he kept firing, firing, firing. Even after we had brought the wounded young men here and moved them away from him, he continued shooting." Nema said young Palestinians threw stones at the settlers after seeing what happened, but asked: "What can stones do against bullets?" The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle". Afterwards, it said, "rocks were hurled at the Israelis, who responded by firing in order to remove the threat." Later, an Israeli military source said Fadda was shot by an Israeli civilian and that there was no evidence that she had been involved in the confrontation near her home. Meanwhile, a spokesperson for Israel's police force said it had opened an investigation, and that officers and forensic technicians had been collecting evidence and interviewing witnesses. The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem says there has been a prolonged campaign of settler attacks, intimidation and land seizures in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, with Israeli troops now stationed nearby to secure the new settlement. Residents and activists say armed settlers walk and drive quad bikes around the neighbourhood as they threaten Palestinian residents. A BBC team saw settlers at the end of the street where Fadda was shot on Tuesday, as well as Israeli flags flying from four of the houses that they had moved into earlier this month. In a separate incident on Monday evening, eight Palestinians were injured when they were hit by a vehicle driven by an Israeli settler on a main road in Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, according to Palestinian officials and the Palestinian Red Crescent. The IDF said the incident was a traffic accident. But the Palestinian foreign ministry called it a "terrorist attack", saying the driver hit a group of Palestinians who had gathered near the scene of an earlier traffic accident. Also on Monday, the Civil Administration - the body that implements Israeli government policy in the West Bank - announced the allocation of more than 28 sq km (6,945 acres) of land in the northern Jordan Valley to nine settlers for grazing, according to the Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now. It said handing over vast tracts of land to settlers for grazing outposts constituted "direct support for the systematic expulsion of Palestinians from their lands and the rampant criminal violence in the West Bank". The UK government announced on Tuesday that it was imposing sanctions on eight companies building Israeli settlements in the West Bank. It is the first sanctions package since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband's pledge in September to respond to the accelerating rate of settlement expansion in the West Bank, which he said risked rendering a two-state solution unviable. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies". Related topics - Published7 days ago

articles.titleTr: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
articles.summaryTr: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".
articles.articleText: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents - Published US President Donald Trump has arrived in the Philippines' capital on the first leg of a trip to Asia, which will end in a meeting in China with its President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. A red carpet was rolled out for Trump as he walked off Air Force One in Manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y.M.C.A., before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel. Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with US partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese. "Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said. "We have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely... my phone is always open," Trump added. Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components. The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China. But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines. Later on Tuesday, Trump signed a trade deal with Thailand alongside the country's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. The US is Thailand's largest export market, accounting for 24% of its total shipments this year. Trump then joined South East Asia leaders at a dinner, telling those gathered: "This is one of the world's most vibrant and productive regions filled with the tremendous potential." After an overnight stay in Manila, the US president will fly to Shenzhen in China to attend a summit of Asia Pacific leaders and have nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Asked if he would also be open to a one-on-one meeting with Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would". - Published7 hours ago - Published11 hours ago

articles.titleTr: Fon soruşturmasında 7 tutuklama daha: Aynı gün ikinci tutuklama kararı
articles.summaryTr: Sermaye piyasalarındaki işlemlere yönelik fon soruşturmasında gözaltına alınan 17 şüpheliden 7'si tutuklandı, 10'u hakkında adli kontrol kararı verildi. Aynı soruşturmada sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı.
articles.articleText: Fon soruşturmasında 7 tutuklama daha: Aynı gün ikinci tutuklama kararı - Sermaye piyasalarındaki işlemlere yönelik fon soruşturmasında gözaltına alınan 17 şüpheliden 7'si tutuklandı, 10'u hakkında adli kontrol kararı verildi. Aynı soruşturmada sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturmasında yeni tutuklama kararları çıktı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınan 17 şüphelinin emniyetteki işlemleri tamamlandı. Sağlık kontrolünden geçirilen şüpheliler, Çağlayan'daki İstanbul Adliyesi'ne sevk edildi. Savcılık ifadelerinin ardından 8 şüpheli tutuklama, 9 şüpheli ise adli kontrol talebiyle sulh ceza hakimliğine gönderildi. Hakimlik, 7 kişinin tutuklanmasına, 10 kişi hakkında ise adli kontrol uygulanmasına karar verdi. Sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı Aynı soruşturma kapsamında daha önce gözaltına alınan 26 şüpheliden 7'si de sabah saatlerinde tutuklanmıştı. Tutuklananlar arasında Ali Kıvanç Mızrakoğlu, Didem Muradoğlu, İlkay Öztürk, İsa Yasin Sevinç, İsmail Erdem, Kazım Erdur ve Hilmi Serhan Çapan yer almıştı. Diğer 19 şüpheli hakkında adli kontrol tedbiri uygulanmıştı. Son kararla birlikte soruşturma kapsamında aynı gün tutuklanan şüpheli sayısı 14'e ulaştı.

articles.titleTr: Asgari ücret zammı enflasyonu geride bıraktı: İspanya'da yeni rakam belli oldu
articles.summaryTr: İspanya hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücreti yüzde 5,3 artırarak aylık brüt 1.286 euroya çıkardı. Yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsayan zam, ülkenin 2026 enflasyon tahminini de geride bıraktı.
articles.articleText: Asgari ücret zammı enflasyonu geride bıraktı: İspanya'da yeni rakam belli oldu - İspanya hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücreti yüzde 5,3 artırarak aylık brüt 1.286 euroya çıkardı. Yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsayan zam, ülkenin 2026 enflasyon tahminini de geride bıraktı. İspanya'da sol azınlık koalisyon hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücrete yüzde 5,3 zam yapılmasını onayladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bakanlar Kurulu'nun aldığı karara göre aylık brüt asgari ücret, 1 Ocak 2027 itibarıyla 1.221 eurodan 1.286 euroya yükselecek. Düzenlemenin yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsaması bekleniyor. Asgari ücretlilerin yılda iki kez tam maaş tutarında ek ödeme aldığı sistemde, bu ücretlerden gelir vergisi kesilmeyecek. Zam oranı enflasyon tahminini aştı Asgari ücrete yapılması kararlaştırılan yüzde 5,3'lük artış, İspanya Merkez Bankası'nın 2026 yılı için öngördüğü yüzde 3,9'luk enflasyon oranının üzerinde gerçekleşti. Zam oranı, ekim itibarıyla son 12 ayda kaydedilen yüzde 4,9'luk enflasyonu da geride bıraktı. Memur maaşlarına da yüzde 4,5 zam İspanya hükümeti, yaklaşık 3 milyon devlet memurunun maaşlarına da yüzde 4,5 zam yapılmasını onayladı. Sendikalarla daha önce varılan anlaşma kapsamında belirlenen artış, 1992'den bu yana memur maaşlarına yapılan en yüksek yıllık zam olacak. Sanchez: 5 milyondan fazla çalışanın ücreti artıyor Başbakan Pedro Sanchez, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada 5 milyondan fazla çalışanın ücretinin artırıldığını belirtti. Sanchez, “Çünkü bunu hak ediyorlar, çünkü ülkemizin ekonomik başarısı aynı zamanda onların çabalarının da bir sonucudur” ifadelerini kullandı. Başbakan Yardımcısı ve Çalışma Bakanı Yolanda Diaz ise sol hükümetin 2018'de göreve gelmesinden bu yana asgari ücretin toplam yüzde 75 artırıldığını açıkladı. Zam için Meclis onayı gerekiyor Hükümetin onayladığı düzenlemenin 1 Ocak 2027'de yürürlüğe girebilmesi için Meclis Daimi Komitesi'nin önümüzdeki günlerde onay vermesi gerekiyor.

Düzenlemenin yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsaması bekleniyor. Asgari ücretlilerin yılda iki kez tam maaş tutarında ek ödeme aldığı sistemde, bu ücretlerden gelir vergisi kesilmeyecek. Zam oranı enflasyon tahminini aştı Asgari ücrete yapılması kararlaştırılan yüzde 5,3'lük artış, İspanya Merkez Bankası'nın 2026 yılı için öngördüğü yüzde 3,9'luk enflasyon oranının üzerinde gerçekleşti. Zam oranı, ekim itibarıyla son 12 ayda kaydedilen yüzde 4,9'luk enflasyonu da geride bıraktı. Memur maaşlarına da yüzde 4,5 zam İspanya hükümeti, yaklaşık 3 milyon devlet memurunun maaşlarına da yüzde 4,5 zam yapılmasını onayladı. Sendikalarla daha önce varılan anlaşma kapsamında belirlenen artış, 1992'den bu yana memur maaşlarına yapılan en yüksek yıllık zam olacak. Sanchez: 5 milyondan fazla çalışanın ücreti artıyor Başbakan Pedro Sanchez, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada 5 milyondan fazla çalışanın ücretinin artırıldığını belirtti. Sanchez, “Çünkü bunu hak ediyorlar, çünkü ülkemizin ekonomik başarısı aynı zamanda onların çabalarının da bir sonucudur” ifadelerini kullandı. Başbakan Yardımcısı ve Çalışma Bakanı Yolanda Diaz ise sol hükümetin 2018'de göreve gelmesinden bu yana asgari ücretin toplam yüzde 75 artırıldığını açıkladı. Zam için Meclis onayı gerekiyor Hükümetin onayladığı düzenlemenin 1 Ocak 2027'de yürürlüğe girebilmesi için Meclis Daimi Komitesi'nin önümüzdeki günlerde onay vermesi gerekiyor.

articles.titleTr: Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ta eş zamanlı kesinti: Milyonlarca kullanıcı etkilendi
articles.summaryTr: Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ın dijital hizmetlerinde 17 Kasım akşamı erişim sorunları yaşandı. Downdetector'a çok sayıda hata bildirimi ulaşırken, kesintilerin ortak bir altyapı sorunundan kaynaklanıp kaynaklanmadığı henüz netleşmedi.
articles.articleText: Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ta eş zamanlı kesinti: Milyonlarca kullanıcı etkilendi - Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'ın dijital hizmetlerinde 17 Kasım akşamı erişim sorunları yaşandı. Downdetector'a çok sayıda hata bildirimi ulaşırken, kesintilerin ortak bir altyapı sorunundan kaynaklanıp kaynaklanmadığı henüz netleşmedi. Teknoloji ve hizmet sektörünün önde gelen şirketleri, 17 Kasım akşamı eş zamanlı erişim sorunlarıyla gündeme geldi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Downdetector verilerine göre Gmail, Apple, Microsoft ve Marriott'a ait çeşitli dijital servislerde kullanıcılar tarafından peş peşe hata bildirimleri yapıldı. Kesintilerin Türkiye saatiyle öğleden sonra ve akşam saatlerinde yoğunlaştığı bildirildi. Gmail ve Marriott kullanıcıları erişim sorunu yaşadı Gmail kullanıcıları e-posta gönderme ve alma işlemlerinde aksaklıklarla karşılaştı. Dünyanın önde gelen otel zincirlerinden Marriott'ın rezervasyon ve giriş sistemlerinde de erişim sorunları rapor edildi. Apple Pay, iCloud ve App Store'da aksaklık Apple ekosisteminde de birden fazla hizmet kesintiden etkilendi. Apple Pay, iCloud, App Store ve Apple Destek hizmetlerinde oturum açma, ödeme yapma ve uygulama indirme işlemlerinde sorunlar yaşandığı bildirildi. Apple'ın resmi sistem durumu sayfası da iCloud hesapları ve giriş işlemlerindeki kesintiyi doğruladı. Microsoft 365 ve Outlook'ta yeni kesinti dalgası Microsoft servislerinde de 17 Kasım öğleden sonra ve akşam saatlerinde hata bildirimleri yeniden yükseldi. Outlook ve Microsoft 365 kullanıcıları erişim ve bağlantı sorunları yaşadıklarını bildirdi. Microsoft, geçtiğimiz hafta 12-14 Kasım tarihlerinde 74 ülkeyi etkileyen büyük altyapı sorununu çözmüştü. Kesintilerin ortak nedeni henüz bilinmiyor Şirketlerin teknik ekipleri hizmetleri normale döndürmek için çalışmalarını sürdürürken, yaşanan aksaklıkların ortak bir küresel altyapı sağlayıcısından mı yoksa birbirinden bağımsız teknik sorunlardan mı kaynaklandığı henüz açıklığa kavuşmadı. Kesintilerin nedenine ilişkin şirketlerden resmi açıklamalar bekleniyor.

articles.articleText: ABD'de peş peşe sistem krizleri: Şimdi de Ulusal Güvelik'in gizli iletişim ağı çöktü - ABD'de havacılık ve bankacılık sistemlerinde yaşanan kesintilerin ardından bu kez Ulusal Güvenlik Ajansı'nın (NSA) kurum içi iletişim ağı devre dışı kaldı. İlk incelemelerde siber saldırı bulgusuna rastlanmadı. ABD'de dijital sistemlerde yaşanan aksaklıklara bir yenisi eklendi. ABD Ulusal Güvenlik Ajansı'nın (NSA) kurum içi iletişimde kullandığı çok gizli ağ devre dışı kaldı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle CNN'in beş kaynağa dayandırdığı haberine göre, ajansın kurum içi iletişim ağında kesinti yaşandı. NSA yetkililerinin sorunun boyutunu anlamaya çalıştığı belirtilirken, şu ana kadar bir siber saldırıya ilişkin herhangi bir bulguya rastlanmadığı aktarıldı. NSA ise kesintiyle ilgili henüz resmi bir açıklama yapmadı. Önce bankalar, ardından havalimanları etkilendi NSA'daki kesinti, ABD'de son günlerde yaşanan diğer sistem arızalarının ardından geldi. Bir gün önce Downdetector, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, US Bank ve Wells Fargo dahil birçok bankanın dijital hizmetlerine erişimde sorunlar yaşandığını bildirmişti. FAA arızası nedeniyle ülke genelinde kalkışlar durmuştu ABD Federal Havacılık İdaresi (FAA), geçtiğimiz cumartesi günü hava trafik kontrol merkezlerini etkileyen bir iletişim arızası nedeniyle ülke genelindeki havalimanlarında kalkışları durdurmuştu. Dört saatten uzun süren durdurma, 11 Eylül 2001 saldırılarından bu yana ABD'de yaşanan en uzun süreli kalkış durdurulması olarak kayıtlara geçmişti.

articles.title: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9327-26 CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading November 17, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today released the agenda for an industry roundtable to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The roundtable is taking place Dec. 15 from 1 to 4 p.m. EST at CFTC Headquarters, Three Lafayette Centre, 1155 21st St., NW, Washington, D.C. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9318-26]. Among other topics, attendees will discuss issues related to the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight and weekend trading, tokenization, margin, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. “From the outset of my chairmanship, I have been clear the CFTC will promote innovation in our derivatives markets in a manner attentive to the nuances of these markets and the varied asset classes that underpin them,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I look forward to hearing directly from industry stakeholders on the ways 24/7 trading would impact their respective business models to ensure the Commission is appropriately tailoring its regulatory regime for all market participants.” View the full agenda here. This meeting is open to the public and will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Dial-in information appears below. For the highest quality, select the number nearest your current location. - New York: 646-828-7666 - New Jersey: 551-285-1373 - San Jose: 669-254-5252 or 669-216-1590 - US toll free: 833-568-8864 or 833-435-1820 - US Spanish-language line: 646-964-1167 or 415-449-4000 - International Numbers - Webinar ID: 165 708 9557 - Passcode: 669856 Individuals with additional questions should contact [email protected]. The views, opinions, and information expressed by roundtable participants are solely those of the respective participants and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Commission, its staff, or the U.S. government. -CFTC-

Selig. “I look forward to hearing directly from industry stakeholders on the ways 24/7 trading would impact their respective business models to ensure the Commission is appropriately tailoring its regulatory regime for all market participants.” View the full agenda here. news.titleTr: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
news.summaryTr: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.
news.articleText: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine - Published Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making. Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort. The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before". Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partially resumed on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - after they had been closed following Russian strikes overnight. Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good. While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin. The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight. The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014. The $3.6bn (£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018. In Ukraine, the much-hated bridge is seen as one of the main symbols of Russia's continuing occupation of Ukrainian lands. "We're drinking champagne!" Andrii, an engineer who lives in Kyiv, told the BBC. He said the latest attack would "deal a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians". Some Ukrainians are concerned that Putin might now respond by carrying out even more attacks against civilian infrastructure, but Andrii said: "I don't think the Russians can make things much worse; they're already pounding us every single night with everything they've got." The damage after the overnight attack, involving cruise missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section apparently destroyed. Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below. Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective". He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage". The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed. Ukraine's state security service SBU said its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders". Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch. The Kremlin said Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China. Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations". For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday. In Kyiv, loud explosions were heard just before midnight on Monday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies. On Tuesday, Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had targeted the Southern Bridge, and another three had been fired on the Northern Bridge. Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were also damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters. Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River, connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials. The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear, though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly. The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired. However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar. This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo. There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack. Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area. In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. In Ukraine, the much-hated bridge is seen as one of the main symbols of Russia's continuing occupation of Ukrainian lands. "We're drinking champagne!" Andrii, an engineer who lives in Kyiv, told the BBC. He said the latest attack would "deal a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians". Some Ukrainians are concerned that Putin might now respond by carrying out even more attacks against civilian infrastructure, but Andrii said: "I don't think the Russians can make things much worse; they're already pounding us every single night with everything they've got." The damage after the overnight attack, involving cruise missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section apparently destroyed. Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below. Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective". He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage". The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed. Ukraine's state security service SBU said its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders". Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch. The Kremlin said Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China. Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations". For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday. In Kyiv, loud explosions were heard just before midnight on Monday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies. On Tuesday, Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had targeted the Southern Bridge, and another three had been fired on the Northern Bridge. Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were also damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters. Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River, connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials. The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear, though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly. The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired. However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar. This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo. There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack. Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area. In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. news.summaryTr: Russia's defence ministry says it preliminarily believes a technical malfunction was the cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.
news.articleText: Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board - Published A Russian military transport plane has crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, the country's defence ministry said, according to state-run media. The An-12 aircraft went down during a "scheduled flight" in an "uninhabited area" in the Kemerovo region, the ministry said in a statement. The ministry added that it preliminarily believed a technical malfunction was the cause of Tuesday's crash. An investigation by Russia's aviation authorities is now under way. Local Governor Ilya Seredyuk said an emergency response team "quickly extinguished a blaze" after the crash near the village of Yagunovo, and the area was sealed off by police. Seredyuk, who visited the crash site, said "a helicopter and medical facilities have been put on standby". The governor added that the "main task" now was to help investigators carry out their work. He also posted a video showing firefighters combing through what looked like the crash debris, with a number of ambulances also seen standing nearby. CCTV footage posted on social media appeared to show the moment the plane crashed, with a lighted object falling through the sky in the distance. An explosion then lit up the sky, but the crash was too far away to be seen. The BBC and Reuters news agency verified the time and date of the footage, while Reuters also verified the location based on features of the scenery that matched satellite imagery of the area. It was not immediately known whether the crashed aircraft had any cargo on board. An-12 planes are widely used by the Russian military to transport weaponry and personnel, and also for search and rescue operations.

news.titleTr: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
news.summaryTr: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.
news.articleText: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers - Published After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months. Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination". The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines. The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s. The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections. The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness. PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year. "These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination." He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission. Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, said that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates. US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr Kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to US vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years. Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections. Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status". "Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency said. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans. "Vaccination does," she said. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities." In a post on social media, Kennedy said: "I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles." "We are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust," he also said. "We will answer families' questions honestly about vaccine benefits and risks and work with trusted health care providers and community leaders to prevent measles, limit its spread, and support timely treatment." The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Nuwan Gunawardhana, an assistant professor of medicine with Columbia University Irving Medical Center, said the US losing its elimination status was "a huge leap backwards". The US was the first country to eliminate measles in the Americas thanks to vaccination campaigns, noted William Moss, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. Dr Gunawardhana said it took massive efforts from public health officials and clinicians to build trust with patients to increase uptake of the MMR vaccine, leading to decades in the US with few infections and deaths. But that trust has been steadily eroding since the Covid-19 pandemic, when Dr Gunawardhana said patients were confronted with misinformation about the safety of vaccines and lost even more trust in public health systems. The vaccination rate for MMR across the US has fallen to 92.4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects those who cannot get vaccinated, including newborns. An outbreak in Pennsylvania has infected over 1,400 people - likely a large underestimate - and killed seven people, according to state officials. Kennedy, the health secretary, has sparred with Pennsylvania officials over how it is counting the measles deaths, with CDC declining for now to record some of the deaths in its database. Last year, the health secretary fired all the members of a top vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with his own appointees, some of whom were vaccine critics. The panel recommended a number of vaccine changes - including no longer requiring the Hepatitis B vaccine for all newborns - but those recommendations were blocked by a federal judge. President Donald Trump this year also cast doubt on the safety of the MMR vaccine, issuing an executive order for the shot to be split into three separate immunisations for measles, mumps and rubella, a move public health experts say is costly and could sow confusion about an already safe vaccine. Doctors and public health officials say the misinformation from Kennedy and Trump has played a major role in falling vaccination rates. "It's confusing patients. It's confusing families," Dr Gunawardhana said. "We need a clear message from the top." The federal government's vaccine manoeuvres have left public health officials and states to fill in the gaps, offering their own separate recommendations upholding decades-long practices. - Published24 July - Published30 January - Published24 September

news.summaryTr: ABD'de FEMA'nın ülke çapındaki acil durum sistemi testi sırasında televizyon ve radyo yayınları kısa süreliğine kesildi. Yaklaşık bir dakika süren testte cep telefonlarına bildirim gönderilmedi.
news.articleText: ABD'de ekranlar karardı, yayınlar kesildi: FEMA ülke çapında acil durum testi yaptı - ABD'de FEMA'nın ülke çapındaki acil durum sistemi testi sırasında televizyon ve radyo yayınları kısa süreliğine kesildi. Yaklaşık bir dakika süren testte cep telefonlarına bildirim gönderilmedi. ABD Federal Acil Durum Yönetim Ajansı (FEMA), ülke genelinde kullanılan Acil Durum Uyarı Sistemi'nin (EAS) işleyişini değerlendirmek amacıyla kapsamlı bir test gerçekleştirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Federal İletişim Komisyonu (FCC) koordinasyonunda yapılan test, ABD Doğu Saati'ne göre 14.20'de başladı. Uygulama kapsamında binlerce televizyon kanalı, radyo istasyonu, kablolu yayın ve uydu hizmeti sağlayıcısının yayınları kısa süreliğine kesildi. İzleyici ve dinleyicilere önce tanıdık acil durum uyarı sesleri iletildi, ardından bunun rutin bir test olduğunu belirten yaklaşık bir dakikalık mesaj yayınlandı. Cep telefonlarına bu kez bildirim gönderilmedi Test kapsamında yalnızca televizyon ve radyo üzerinden çalışan Acil Durum Uyarı Sistemi değerlendirildi. Cep telefonlarına doğrudan gönderilen Kablosuz Acil Durum Uyarıları (WEA) ise bu yılki uygulamanın dışında bırakıldı. 2023 yılında gerçekleştirilen son ülke çapındaki testte hem televizyon ve radyo yayınları hem de cep telefonu bildirimleri kullanılmıştı. Amaç ulusal acil durumlarda iletişimi güvence altına almak FEMA'nın gerçekleştirdiği testle, ulusal acil durumlarda halkın hızlı ve doğru bilgilendirilmesini sağlayan iletişim altyapısının güvenilirliği ölçüldü. Sistem; ulusal güvenlik tehditleri, şiddetli hava olayları, tahliye kararları ve kamu güvenliğini ilgilendiren diğer acil gelişmelerde yetkililerin halka ulaşmasını sağlıyor. news.titleTr: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
news.summaryTr: The Metropolitan Police say he has been taken into custody by the US Military over suspected national security and espionage allegations.
news.articleText: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody - Published A US Army officer arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia earlier this month has been taken into US military custody, British counter-terror police have said. The serviceman has been identified as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, BBC News understands. The 41-year-old - who has served in the US Army since 2008 - was arrested near Gloucester last week by British counter-terror police. Tyner was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC). Counter Terror Policing said he is now in custody over suspected national security and espionage allegations. At the time of his arrest, Russia said they had "nothing to do with it". British police previously said he was being held in London after he was arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023, which relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service. The day after Tyner's arrest, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he was "unaware" of what it was connected to. "We have nothing to do with it, and it has nothing to do with us," he told reporters in Moscow. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said: "Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them [their American partners] to progress." "These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," he added. FBI director Kash Patel said an army officer was in custody "as the result of an espionage investigation and the close cooperation" between the bureau, US Army and various UK partners. "Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action," he said. "This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk." US Brig Gen Sean Stinchon said the case should serve as a "stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath" they all take. "Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardising our collective defence, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served," he added. news.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
news.summary: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.

news.titleTr: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
news.summaryTr: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
news.articleText: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says - Published A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says. There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority. According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman. There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost. They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control. All settlements are illegal under international law. - UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements - Published3 hours ago Local Palestinians said that the events in al-Duyuk al-Tahta on Monday night began with harassment by Israeli settlers. Palestinian children threw stones, they said, and the settlers opened fire, killing Fadda al-Fahidat, who was 72, outside her home. Fadda's daughter-in-law, Nema al-Fahidat, told the BBC that she died from a single bullet wound to the head. "It destroyed her brain," she said. According to the Palestinian accounts, Fadda's son, Arafat, rushed to the scene in his car after hearing the news and collided with an empty Israeli settler car parked outside his family home, injuring settlers who were standing nearby. The settlers then fired more shots, they said, injuring several Palestinians, including Arafat. "My husband, when he saw his mother, was not paying attention. He crashed into the vehicle. The vehicle was empty," Nema said. "My husband got out of his car and tried to reach his mother and the injured young men. Then he was shot." She added: "We tried to gather the injured people and move them away from the settler. We brought them here. But he kept firing, firing, firing. Even after we had brought the wounded young men here and moved them away from him, he continued shooting." Nema said young Palestinians threw stones at the settlers after seeing what happened, but asked: "What can stones do against bullets?" The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle". Afterwards, it said, "rocks were hurled at the Israelis, who responded by firing in order to remove the threat." Later, an Israeli military source said Fadda was shot by an Israeli civilian and that there was no evidence that she had been involved in the confrontation near her home. Meanwhile, a spokesperson for Israel's police force said it had opened an investigation, and that officers and forensic technicians had been collecting evidence and interviewing witnesses. The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem says there has been a prolonged campaign of settler attacks, intimidation and land seizures in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, with Israeli troops now stationed nearby to secure the new settlement. Residents and activists say armed settlers walk and drive quad bikes around the neighbourhood as they threaten Palestinian residents. A BBC team saw settlers at the end of the street where Fadda was shot on Tuesday, as well as Israeli flags flying from four of the houses that they had moved into earlier this month. In a separate incident on Monday evening, eight Palestinians were injured when they were hit by a vehicle driven by an Israeli settler on a main road in Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, according to Palestinian officials and the Palestinian Red Crescent. The IDF said the incident was a traffic accident. But the Palestinian foreign ministry called it a "terrorist attack", saying the driver hit a group of Palestinians who had gathered near the scene of an earlier traffic accident. Also on Monday, the Civil Administration - the body that implements Israeli government policy in the West Bank - announced the allocation of more than 28 sq km (6,945 acres) of land in the northern Jordan Valley to nine settlers for grazing, according to the Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now. It said handing over vast tracts of land to settlers for grazing outposts constituted "direct support for the systematic expulsion of Palestinians from their lands and the rampant criminal violence in the West Bank". The UK government announced on Tuesday that it was imposing sanctions on eight companies building Israeli settlements in the West Bank. It is the first sanctions package since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband's pledge in September to respond to the accelerating rate of settlement expansion in the West Bank, which he said risked rendering a two-state solution unviable. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies". Related topics - Published7 days ago

news.titleTr: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
news.summaryTr: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".
news.articleText: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents - Published US President Donald Trump has arrived in the Philippines' capital on the first leg of a trip to Asia, which will end in a meeting in China with its President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. A red carpet was rolled out for Trump as he walked off Air Force One in Manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y.M.C.A., before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel. Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with US partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese. "Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said. "We have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely... my phone is always open," Trump added. Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components. The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China. But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines. Later on Tuesday, Trump signed a trade deal with Thailand alongside the country's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. The US is Thailand's largest export market, accounting for 24% of its total shipments this year. Trump then joined South East Asia leaders at a dinner, telling those gathered: "This is one of the world's most vibrant and productive regions filled with the tremendous potential." After an overnight stay in Manila, the US president will fly to Shenzhen in China to attend a summit of Asia Pacific leaders and have nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Asked if he would also be open to a one-on-one meeting with Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would". - Published7 hours ago - Published11 hours ago

A red carpet was rolled out for Trump as he walked off Air Force One in Manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y.M.C.A., before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel. Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with US partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese. "Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said. "We have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely... my phone is always open," Trump added. Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components. The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China. But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines. Later on Tuesday, Trump signed a trade deal with Thailand alongside the country's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. The US is Thailand's largest export market, accounting for 24% of its total shipments this year. Trump then joined South East Asia leaders at a dinner, telling those gathered: "This is one of the world's most vibrant and productive regions filled with the tremendous potential." Savcılık ifadelerinin ardından 8 şüpheli tutuklama, 9 şüpheli ise adli kontrol talebiyle sulh ceza hakimliğine gönderildi. Hakimlik, 7 kişinin tutuklanmasına, 10 kişi hakkında ise adli kontrol uygulanmasına karar verdi. Sabah saatlerinde de 7 kişi tutuklanmıştı Aynı soruşturma kapsamında daha önce gözaltına alınan 26 şüpheliden 7'si de sabah saatlerinde tutuklanmıştı. news.titleTr: Asgari ücret zammı enflasyonu geride bıraktı: İspanya'da yeni rakam belli oldu
news.summaryTr: İspanya hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücreti yüzde 5,3 artırarak aylık brüt 1.286 euroya çıkardı. Yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsayan zam, ülkenin 2026 enflasyon tahminini de geride bıraktı.
news.articleText: Asgari ücret zammı enflasyonu geride bıraktı: İspanya'da yeni rakam belli oldu - İspanya hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücreti yüzde 5,3 artırarak aylık brüt 1.286 euroya çıkardı. Yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsayan zam, ülkenin 2026 enflasyon tahminini de geride bıraktı. İspanya'da sol azınlık koalisyon hükümeti, 2027 yılı için asgari ücrete yüzde 5,3 zam yapılmasını onayladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bakanlar Kurulu'nun aldığı karara göre aylık brüt asgari ücret, 1 Ocak 2027 itibarıyla 1.221 eurodan 1.286 euroya yükselecek. Düzenlemenin yaklaşık 2,7 milyon çalışanı kapsaması bekleniyor. Asgari ücretlilerin yılda iki kez tam maaş tutarında ek ödeme aldığı sistemde, bu ücretlerden gelir vergisi kesilmeyecek. Zam oranı enflasyon tahminini aştı Asgari ücrete yapılması kararlaştırılan yüzde 5,3'lük artış, İspanya Merkez Bankası'nın 2026 yılı için öngördüğü yüzde 3,9'luk enflasyon oranının üzerinde gerçekleşti. Zam oranı, ekim itibarıyla son 12 ayda kaydedilen yüzde 4,9'luk enflasyonu da geride bıraktı. Memur maaşlarına da yüzde 4,5 zam İspanya hükümeti, yaklaşık 3 milyon devlet memurunun maaşlarına da yüzde 4,5 zam yapılmasını onayladı. Sendikalarla daha önce varılan anlaşma kapsamında belirlenen artış, 1992'den bu yana memur maaşlarına yapılan en yüksek yıllık zam olacak. Sanchez: 5 milyondan fazla çalışanın ücreti artıyor Başbakan Pedro Sanchez, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada 5 milyondan fazla çalışanın ücretinin artırıldığını belirtti. Sanchez, “Çünkü bunu hak ediyorlar, çünkü ülkemizin ekonomik başarısı aynı zamanda onların çabalarının da bir sonucudur” ifadelerini kullandı. Başbakan Yardımcısı ve Çalışma Bakanı Yolanda Diaz ise sol hükümetin 2018'de göreve gelmesinden bu yana asgari ücretin toplam yüzde 75 artırıldığını açıkladı. Zam için Meclis onayı gerekiyor Hükümetin onayladığı düzenlemenin 1 Ocak 2027'de yürürlüğe girebilmesi için Meclis Daimi Komitesi'nin önümüzdeki günlerde onay vermesi gerekiyor.
